source: Estimating Reproductive Numbers Zimbabwe Cholera PNAS PMC3102413
processing_notes: Source states: 'Zimbabwe has experienced sporadic outbreaks of cholera since the introduction of seventh pandemic El Tor strains in the 1970s' but confirms first documented large outbreak only in 1992. Academic sources confirm the 1977-1984 period was not documented with cholera cases in the formal surveillance record. Absence inferred from: (1) first large documented outbreak in 1992, (2) RSTMH paper confirms 'reappeared for first time since 1985' in 1992 suggesting no cases after 1985. Zero-transmission evidence: Inferred_Absence from gap analysis with regional context. Surveillance system status: pre-independence Zimbabwe (Rhodesia until 1980) had limited formal health surveillance.
retracted_reason: RETRACTED by Agent 1: directly contradicted by evidence. This row asserted sCh=0 and deaths=0 across the whole of 1973-01-01..1984-12-31 as an Inferred_Absence. Cruickshank JG, Farrell HB and Ellis BP published an entire supplement of The Central African Journal of Medicine (1975 Jan;21(1 Suppl):1-10, PMID 1111974) titled 'Cholera in the Manicaland Province of Rhodesia February to May, 1974', so cholera was demonstrably present in Zimbabwe/Rhodesia inside the asserted absence window. The absence was never documented in the first place: its own note derived it from a 1992 paper saying cholera 'reappeared for the first time since 1985' plus the absence of records, and the authoritative MoHCC series (Multi-Sectoral Cholera Elimination Plan Table 4, 'Cholera Cases and Deaths in Zimbabwe, 1972 - March 2019') leaves 1973-1981 BLANK while stating explicitly that 'Blank spaces mean no data' - i.e. non-reporting, not zero. A 12-year asserted zero built on missing records is exactly the false negative the zero-transmission protocol forbids. The 1974 Manicaland outbreak is instead recorded in data/ZWE/cholera_presence_ai.csv, and 1973-1984 is left genuinely empty for Agent 3 or Agent 4 to re-examine.
